_meta: A short token sequence, used to show why a next-token language model's target at each position must be the NEXT token (position i+1), not the token at the same position (i) -- and why the same-position objective is trivially cheatable and teaches nothing. A language model is trained by teacher forcing: it reads a prefix of tokens and predicts the following token. To build the training pairs you shift the targets by one relative to the inputs -- the label for the model's output at position i is tokens[i+1]. The classic bug is to line up the outputs with the inputs at the SAME position, so the target for position i is tokens[i]: the model is asked to predict a token that (under a correct causal mask) it can already see at that position. That objective is satisfied by the identity function -- just copy the input to the output -- so a model that learns nothing about language scores a perfect loss, and at generation time it has learned only to echo. The fix is the one-token shift: inputs are tokens[:-1] and targets are tokens[1:], so predicting position i means predicting tokens[i+1] from tokens[0..i], a genuine prediction the model cannot cheat by copying. This is separate from the causal mask: the mask decides what the model may attend to; the label shift decides what it is asked to predict. A model with a correct mask but unshifted labels still learns the wrong task. tokens is the fixture sequence; the two alignments (same-position vs shifted-by-one) and the accuracy of a copy model on each are computed.
